mechanism.summary: T057 stage 1 (docs/design/string-code-units.md): preserve the shared JsString handle through typed receiver/ToString coercion and the RegExp symbol-method protocols (match, matchAll iterator, search, replace custom-exec loop, string-needle replace callbacks), so repeated exec calls on one subject reuse its memoized matcher view instead of copying the subject and rebuilding the view per call; answer String search boundary helpers (indexOf/includes/startsWith/endsWith) from the memoized ASCII classification instead of rescanning the subject on every call; count the subject once per string-needle replacement instead of once per match. Wide indexing, storage and the legacy non-ASCII scalar search coordinates stay unchanged.
mechanism.generality: Admission depends only on value types and data flow: any primitive string or String wrapper receiver, any ToString argument that is already a string, any RegExp-like object whose exec is called repeatedly on one subject, and any ASCII subject searched with a cursor. No source, pattern or library shape is recognized.
semantic_risks: ToPrimitive/toString/valueOf hook order and count must be unchanged for non-string arguments
Every Get(exec), Get(flags), Get/Set(lastIndex) and species lookup in the RegExp protocols must still be observed per call
The non-ASCII legacy search branch must keep its scalar coordinates; unit lengths must never be mixed with scalar offsets
Custom exec and replacement callbacks receive a string equal to the subject; sharing must not expose mutation or alias metadata
Memoized matcher views retained on long-lived subjects must not change results when Unicode modes alternate
